content:
Here is a cautious line‑by‑line translation, keeping close to the Sumerian and noting where the text is broken or uncertain. Bracketed sections […] are damaged or missing; parentheses indicate explanatory additions.

1. ud re-a-ta ud an ki-bi-ta ba-an-dim2-ma-ba  
   “From the first day, the day was (thus) determined from (the relationship of) heaven and earth.”

2. ĝi6 re-a-ta ĝi6 an ki-bi-ta ba-an-dim2-ma-ba  
   “From the first night, the night was (thus) determined from (the relationship of) heaven and earth.”

3. [mu re]-a-ta mu nam ba-tar-ra-ba  
   “[From the first year], the year’s fate (destiny) was decreed.”

4. [da]-nun-na-ke4-ne ba-tu-ud-da-a-ba  
   “The Anunna-gods were born (were brought forth).”

5. dama-dinana nam-NIR.PA-še3 ba-tuku-a-ba  
   “Inanna, lady, acquired (took possession of) the office of NIR.PA (a cultic/ritual prerogative).”

6. dama-dinana an ki-a ba-ḫal-ḫal-la-a-ba  
   “Inanna, lady, joyously traversed / roamed heaven and earth.”

7. dama-dinana […] ba-a-peš u3-tud-da-a-ba  
   “Inanna, lady, […] she grew stout/robust and gave birth (bore offspring).”

8. diĝir kurum6-ma-bi A X X unu2?-bi-še3 ba-ab-keše2-a-ba  
   “The god of that city/region, its water‑(something) and (its) shrine(?) they bound together for it.”

9. diĝir šar2-šar2 kiĝ2-ĝa2 al-sug2-ge-eš diĝir tur-tur du2-lum im-il2-il2-e-ne  
   “The gods of abundance, who enrich my things, the small gods, the minor ones, they carried (them) off.”

10. diĝir id2 im dun-dun-u3-ne saḫar-bi ḫa-ra-li im-dub-dub-be2-ne  
    “The river‑gods, they kept pounding (roaring); its dust they kept piling up.”

11. diĝir im ar3-ar3-re-ne zi-bi inim am3-ma-ĝar-re-ne  
    “The storm‑gods, as they kept raging, they set therein the (living) breath and the word (decree).”

12. ud-ba ĝeštug2 daĝal mud diĝir šar2-šar2 ĝal2-ĝal2  
    “On that day, broad understanding and wisdom (were present); the great gods of abundance existed.”

13. den-ki-ke4 engur buru3 a-sur-ra ki diĝir na-me šag4-bi u6 nu-um-me  
    “Enki, (in) the subterranean waters, in the brimming apsû, in the place of the far‑flowing water—no god at all knew its interior.”

14. ki-nu2-ni i3-nu2 u3 ku nu-um-zi-zi  
    “On his resting‑place he lay down, and he did not rise from sleep.”

15. diĝir er2-ra im-pad-pad-ne a-nir ĝal2 i3-ak im-me-ne  
    “The lamenting gods cried out; ‘There is abundant lament‑water!’—thus they said.”

16. lu2 ku-ra i3-nu2-a-ra ki-nu2-bi nu-um-zi-zi-ra  
    “When the man of (that) quarrel/conflict lay down there, his resting‑place did not let him rise.”

17. dnamma-ke4 ama palil u3-tud diĝir šar2-šar2-ra-ke4-ne  
    “Namma, the mother who bore Palil and the gods of abundance …”

18. er2-ra diĝir-re-e-ne dumu-ni-ir ba-ši-in-de6  
    “The lamenting gods—her children—she bore (gave birth to).”

19. X mu-un-ši-nu2-u3-nam u3 mu-un-ši-ku-ku-na-nam  
    “She made them lie down in X, and she made them stand up(?) in …” (exact sense uncertain due to the break)

20. [X] TE BA [… nu-mu-un]-zi-zi  
    “[When] X had been destroyed/finished, … he/they did not rise.”  

21. dim3-me2-er šu dim2-dim2-ma-zu X gu2?-bi im-tu10-tu10-ne  
    “Dim-me-er, with your fashioned hands they (kept) polishing / making pleasant its X (possibly ‘neck’, ‘base’, or ‘mound’).”

Because the text is damaged in several places and uses some specialized cultic / cosmological vocabulary (e.g., NIR.PA, engur, a‑sur‑ra), a fully smooth literary translation is not possible for every line, but this captures the most likely meanings given the preserved Sumerian.
